mechanism_narrative: Sustained improvement in WORKPLACES mobility (rising from -28.6% to -17.7% over 3 weeks) signals resumption of commuting patterns. Commuters generate incidental retail visits during work-week travel, driving RETAIL_REC higher over the next four weeks.
evidence_refs: fact:WORKPLACES improved 10.9 percentage points from t-2w to t-0w
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC mean over next 28 days does not exceed RETAIL_REC mean over prior 28 days, or WORKPLACES reverses to decline in week t+1.

mechanism_narrative: TRANSIT station mobility remains severely depressed (−49.7%), indicating persistent avoidance of public transport. This suppresses retail-recreation visits that depend on transit access, keeping RETAIL_REC negative over the next four weeks.
evidence_refs: fact:TRANSIT at −49.7% in t-0w, only 7 percentage points above t-3w low
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC mean over next 28 days exceeds RETAIL_REC mean over prior 28 days, or TRANSIT rises above −30% in week t+1.

mechanism_narrative: PARKS mobility has stabilized near −14% after sharp decline from −19.9%, indicating outdoor recreation demand has plateaued. This plateau in outdoor substitutes removes downward pressure on RETAIL_REC, allowing retail-recreation to recover toward baseline over the next two weeks.
candidate_trigger: PARKS week-on-week change magnitude falls below 3 percentage points
evidence_refs: fact:PARKS improved 5.9 points from t-2w to t-0w, then stabilized
failure_condition: PARKS continues to decline or RETAIL_REC does not improve by at least 2 percentage points in weeks t+1 and t+2.

mechanism_narrative: Concurrent improvement in both WORKPLACES (−17.7%) and TRANSIT (−49.7%) creates a two-factor demand signal: workers returning to offices generate retail footfall, while transit recovery enables multi-stop shopping trips. The interaction amplifies RETAIL_REC gains over four weeks.
candidate_trigger: WORKPLACES and TRANSIT both improve week-on-week in same period
evidence_refs: fact:WORKPLACES improved 10.9 points and TRANSIT improved 7.2 points from t-2w to t-0w
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC mean over next 28 days does not exceed prior 28-day mean, or either WORKPLACES or TRANSIT reverses to decline in week t+1.

mechanism_narrative: RESIDENTIAL mobility remains elevated (6.1%) relative to pre-pandemic baseline, indicating continued work-from-home prevalence. Persistent remote work suppresses commute-linked retail visits, keeping RETAIL_REC depressed below −10% over the next four weeks.
candidate_trigger: RESIDENTIAL remains above 5% for two consecutive weeks
evidence_refs: fact:RESIDENTIAL at 6.1% in t-0w, consistently 6−10% across all four weeks
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC mean over next 28 days exceeds RETAIL_REC mean over prior 28 days, or RESIDENTIAL falls below 3% in week t+1.

mechanism_narrative: GROCERY_PHARM mobility has stabilized at 0.6−0.7%, indicating essential shopping is at steady state with no growth. Absence of grocery-driven foot traffic spillover to adjacent retail means RETAIL_REC cannot leverage grocery momentum, constraining recovery to one week horizon.
candidate_trigger: GROCERY_PHARM remains within ±1 percentage point for two consecutive weeks
evidence_refs: fact:GROCERY_PHARM at 0.6−0.7% across t-2w, t-1w, t-0w with no trend
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC rises above −10% in week t+1, or GROCERY_PHARM rises above 2% in week t+1.

mechanism_narrative: Convergence of four mobility series toward baseline (RETAIL_REC −13.9%, WORKPLACES −17.7%, TRANSIT −49.7%, PARKS −14.0%) indicates transition from acute restriction regime to endemic steady state. In this regime, retail-recreation demand stabilizes and begins recovery toward baseline over four weeks.
candidate_trigger: variance of four-week mean changes across RETAIL_REC, WORKPLACES, TRANSIT, PARKS falls below 5 percentage points
evidence_refs: fact:all four series show week-on-week improvement from t-2w to t-0w
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC mean over next 28 days does not exceed prior 28-day mean, or any of the four series reverses sharply in week t+1.

This two-factor constraint keeps RETAIL_REC suppressed over the next two weeks unless TRANSIT recovers above −40%.
evidence_refs: fact:RESIDENTIAL at 6.1% and TRANSIT at −49.7% in t-0w
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC mean over next 14 days exceeds RETAIL_REC mean over prior 14 days, or TRANSIT rises above −40% in week t+1.
